q1: SELECT NAME AS CUSTOMERS FROM CUSTOMERS WHERE ID NOT IN (SELECT CUSTOMERID FROM ORDERS)
q2: SELECT A.NAME CUSTOMERS FROM CUSTOMERS A WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT B.CUSTOMERID FROM ORDERS B WHERE A.ID=B.CUSTOMERID)
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT NAME AS CUSTOMERS FROM CUSTOMERS WHERE ID NOT IN (SELECT CUSTOMERID FROM ORDERS)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT A.NAME CUSTOMERS FROM CUSTOMERS A WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT B.CUSTOMERID FROM ORDERS B WHERE A.ID=B.CUSTOMERID)
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are semantically equivalent. Both queries retrieve the names of customers who have not placed any orders. Q1 uses NOT IN with a subquery, while Q2 uses NOT EXISTS with a correlated subquery. In this specific case, they produce the same result because the subquery in Q1 returns a single column (CUSTOMERID) that matches the type of the outer query's column (ID).
